reason: Cooling in the carbon-bearing outflow could allow carbon dust to form.
expectation: Carbon-bearing grains should condense as the wind cools.

effect: The cooled stellar wind produced carbonaceous grains, providing the carbon-bearing dust needed for the goal.
reaction: It is satisfying to see the wind become solid grains.
reason: The stellar ejecta may also form grains as they cool, potentially supplying rock-forming material.
expectation: Cooling the ejecta may produce rock-forming grains.

effect: The ejecta instead drove a shock into primordial gas; cooling the outflow was not the direct route to rock grains.
reaction: The shock was an unexpected but useful intermediate.
reason: The shock is a newly available intermediate, and its next useful partner is not obvious.
expectation: Inspection should reveal how the shocked gas can contribute to the dust-forming cloud.

effect: Radiation cooled the shocked gas into an enriched cloud, suggesting a reservoir for forming dust.
reaction: The link between radiative cooling and mixing is useful to see.
reason: The enriched cloud is the new intermediate, but its route to rock-forming grains is not yet clear.
expectation: Inspection should reveal what can form from the cooling cloud.

effect: The cooling cloud mixed with stellar wind material, producing a cloud enriched by multiple stellar sources.
reaction: The multiple-source origin is a useful clarification.
reason: The enriched cloud is the latest intermediate, and its next partner is not obvious.

choice.inspect: A cloud enriched by a stellar wind

expectation: Inspection should reveal the next available step toward forming mixed dust.

effect: The cloud now contains a mixed supply of rock-forming, metallic and carbon elements from multiple stellar generations.
reaction: The distinction between a mixed reservoir and a single star's ejecta is helpful.
reason: The mixed element supply is the new intermediate, but its next partner is unclear.
expectation: Inspection should reveal how the mixed elements can form dust grains.

effect: Cooling the mixed element supply produced iron-bearing metal grains, but the rock-forming grain goal remains unresolved.
reaction: The distinction between tiny grains and miniature planets is helpful.
reason: The mixed element supply may have another route to rock-forming grains, so checking its remaining partners is useful.
expectation: Inspection should reveal any remaining available combinations for the element supply.

effect: The mixed element supply has no remaining available combinations, so I need another route to rock-forming grains.
reaction: That rules out the intermediate I had hoped to reuse.
reason: Carbon-rich stellar material remains available, but its relevance to the unfinished dust goals is unclear.
expectation: Inspection should reveal whether it has an available role in forming the remaining dust.

effect: Carbon-rich stellar material produced oxygen-rich material, offering a possible route to rock-forming grains.
reaction: The nuclear origin of oxygen is a useful connection.
reason: The new oxygen-rich material may have a route to rock-forming dust, but its partner is unclear.
expectation: Inspection should reveal how the oxygen-rich material can contribute to the remaining goals.

effect: Oxygen-rich material and the mixed element supply produced silicate-forming vapor, a precursor to rocky minerals.
reaction: The connection between oxygen, silicon and magnesium makes the route to rock clearer.
reason: Cooling the silicate-forming vapor should allow rock-forming grains to condense.
expectation: The vapor should cool into silicate grains.

effect: Cooling the vapor produced silicate grains, the microscopic mineral material needed for rock.
reaction: The progression from vapor to tiny grains makes the origin of rock tangible.
reason: The silicate and iron-bearing grains could form a mixed stock of rocky and metallic dust.
expectation: The grains may combine into a mixed dust stock.

effect: Silicate and iron-bearing grains formed rock-forming dust, completing the first goal.
reaction: The possibility that the materials can separate again after melting is interesting.
reason: Combining the rock-forming dust with the carbonaceous grains should bring carbon into the mixed dust.

choice.with: Carbonaceous grains from a stellar wind

expectation: The grains should form a dust mixture containing rock, metal and carbon.

effect: The carbonaceous grains joined the rock-forming dust to make mixed interstellar dust, completing the remaining goal.
reaction: The reminder that dust is only a small fraction of the gas puts the finished mixture in useful context.

mostWorthwhile.text: Making silicate grains from vapor made the origin of rock tangible: cooling produces microscopic minerals long before a rocky world exists.

leastWorthwhile.text: Reinspecting the mixed element supply found no partners and did not advance the goals, though it ruled out my intended route.

surprise.text: The ejecta did not directly form grains when paired with cooling; they drove a shock into surrounding gas instead.

arbitrary.text: The connection between carbon-rich stellar material and neutral helium was not obvious to me until inspection revealed it, although the result explained oxygen production.

continue.text: Yes. I would be curious to follow how these microscopic grains and the much larger gas reservoir contribute to planets; the chapter made the physical progression understandable.
